5599.prule: Stress is predictable and fixed on the root ('relatively weak, word boundary stress: on root'); Syangja Magar is coded as keeping this Tibeto-Burman pattern rather than the Nepali one.
5599.quote: In the Bodic groupings in our sample, stress was predictable and was generally fixed on the root. Where languages have borrowed large amounts of Nepali vocabulary, they have accommodated to the Nepali stress pattern. … Kham: T.Magar: S.Magar: … stress +T/-N +T/-N +T/-N +T/-N +T/-N … +T/-N = consistent with the structural profile of the grouping and not consonant with Nepali

tn.quote: （三）聲調 1. 高平，寫作˥（55）；例如 bγ˥ '揹' 2. 中平，寫作˧（33）；例如 bγ˧ '蟲' 3. 低平，寫作˩（11）；例如 bγ˩ '漂流' 4. 短調，寫作˨（2）；例如 bγ˨ '菩薩' 註：短調˨(2) 是很短的調子，在這個短調的後面收喉頭塞音〔ʔ〕，因爲喉頭塞音是這個調子的附屬品，所以我們就不寫他了。單字調和別的詞連讀時，往往變調，普通所見的大概否定詞 ma˩ '不' 和 t'a˩ '莫' 後面若跟有高平調˥(55)的動詞，就要降成中平調˧(33) … 還有表示擬定的口氣，往往將句中之動詞變成低升調 …
tn.translation: (3) Tones. 1. High level, written ˥ (55); e.g. bγ˥ 'carry on the back'. 2. Mid level, written ˧ (33); e.g. bγ˧ 'insect'. 3. Low level, written ˩ (11); e.g. bγ˩ 'drift'. 4. Short tone, written ˨ (2); e.g. bγ˨ 'Bodhisattva'. Note: the short tone (2) is a very short tone; after it the syllable closes in a glottal stop [ʔ]; since the glottal stop is an appendage of this tone we do not write it. When citation tones are read together with other words there is often tone sandhi: the negatives ma˩ 'not' and t'a˩ 'don't', if followed by a high-level (55) verb, lower it to mid level (33) … and to express a hypothetical mood the verb of the clause is often changed to a low rising tone …
tn.cite: Ma Xueliang [馬學良]. 1948. 倮文作祭獻藥供牲經譯註 [Annotated translation of the Lolo scripture for offering medicine and sacrifice at the memorial rite]. 中央研究院歷史語言研究所集刊 (Bulletin of the Institute of History and Philology, Academia Sinica) 20: 577 ff.
tn.locator: p. 579, sec. 二 標音說明, (三) 聲調 and its 註
tn.note: Four tones: high level 55, mid level 33, low level 11, and a very short tone 2 closed by a glottal stop; laryngealised vowels are a vowel feature; 55 lowers to 33 after the negatives.

tn.quote: Underlyingly, Wushi has four tones: two level tones H (high) and L (low) inherited from the proto language – they were reconstructed for Proto-Grassfields (Watters 2003: 236) – and two contour tones that were phonologized in the language, LH (rising) and HL (falling). Surface tones are H, L, M (mid), HL (falling), LH (rising), and HM, plus downstepped ꜜH, ꜜM and ꜜHM. … The mora is the tone bearing unit in the language. … In Wushi like in all the other Ring languages, the mid tone is phonetic.
tn.cite: Hodieb, Liliane. 2024. On the syntax-prosody interface in Wushi (Babessi): Tone pattern, dissimilation and spreading. In James Essegbey, Brent Henderson, Fiona McLaughlin & Michael Diercks (eds.), Pushing the boundaries: Selected papers from the 51-52 Annual Conference on African Linguistics (Contemporary African Linguistics), 163-184. Berlin: Language Science Press. doi:10.5281/zenodo.14038745

tn.note: Four underlying tones, high, low, rising and falling, borne by the mora; surface mid, HM and downstepped tones arise from floating tones; noun-class affixes are toneless and copy root tone.

refs.ref: Creissels, Denis. 1989. Structures syllabiques du dialonké de Faléya. Mandenkan 18: 1-30.

5603.loc: sect. 7 'Règles tonales et structures syllabiques', pp. 20-21
5603.idn: Name in the source: dialonké (dialonké de Faléya); family in the source: langue mandé-nord, apparentée de très près au soso (Creissels 1989, Keita 1989); Mande, Western branch, Susu-Jalonke group 'группа сусу-дьялонке' (Vydrin 2017); the statement concerns a variety of this language

tn.quote: Le dialonké a un système tonal réductible à deux unités tonologiques de base, |H| et |B|, et les tons lexicaux du dialonké coïncident presque toujours avec ceux du soso, dont le dialonké est dans l'ensemble très proche. Mais le dialonké se distingue du soso par la complexité de ses règles de réalisation tonale. … on constate en effet que les syllabes CV ne peuvent être associés qu'à un unique ton simple (H ou B), tandis que les syllabes CV: aussi bien que CVC peuvent être associées à une séquence tonale HB ou BH. Par exemple: kwɛ́ɛ̀ "nuit", sún ̀ "jeûne",tàá "village", sàn ́ "jambe"
tn.translation: Dialonké has a tonal system reducible to two basic tonological units, |H| and |L|, and the lexical tones of Dialonké almost always coincide with those of Soso, to which Dialonké is on the whole very close. But Dialonké differs from Soso in the complexity of its tone-realisation rules. … one observes that CV syllables can only be associated with a single simple tone (H or L), whereas CV: as well as CVC syllables can be associated with a tonal sequence HL or LH. For example: kwɛ́ɛ̀ 'night', sún ̀ 'fast', tàá 'village', sàn ́ 'leg'
tn.cite: Creissels, Denis. 1989. Structures syllabiques du dialonké de Faléya. Mandenkan 18: 1-30.
tn.locator: sect. 7 'Règles tonales et structures syllabiques', pp. 20-21
tn.note: Two level tones, high and low (Faléya dialect, Mali); words carry set schemes (H, HL, LH, LHL); a floating low downsteps a following high. The Fouta Djallon variety described by Lüpke has lost tone.

tn.quote: There is evidence for a three-way tonal opposition in Kabarasi: H vs. ∅ vs. L. The primary contrast is between H and ∅; virtually all tonal generalizations for Kabarasi can be stated with reference only to the presence vs. absence of Hs. … This is the only known evidence for phonological L in Kabarasi at this time. The tone bearing unit (TBU) is the mora in Kabarasi. … contour tones are not phonological primitives, but emerge when only one mora within a heavy syllable bears an H.
tn.cite: Ebarb, Kristopher J. 2016. An overview of Kabarasi verb tone. Language 92(3): e134-e191 (Phonological Analysis). Linguistic Society of America. doi:10.1353/lan.2016.0054
tn.locator: p. e135, sec. 1 Introduction
tn.note: Verb roots contrast H vs toneless, plus a marginal L on some prefixes; the mora bears tone and contours are not primitives; downstep between adjacent Hs; eight inflectional melodic-H patterns.

5613.idn: Name in the source: mbuun (B87); Mbuun (Mbunda); parlers d'Imbongo; parler d'Idiofa

tn.quote: La langue mbuun a recours à deux tons simples H et B. Les réalisations contextuelles de ces deux tons en modulation conduisent à des tons montants et descendants. Ces tons modulés résultent des contacts entre deux tons simples. Le ton descendant est plus fréquent que le ton montant. Toutefois, malgré le défaut de paires minimales opposant le ton descendant au ton montant, nous pensons que le mbuun a quatre registres tonals: H, B et HB (descendant) et BH (montant).
tn.translation: The Mbuun language uses two simple tones, H and L. The contextual realisations of these two tones in modulation lead to rising and falling tones. These modulated tones result from contacts between two simple tones. The falling tone is more frequent than the rising tone. However, despite the lack of minimal pairs opposing the falling tone to the rising tone, we think that Mbuun has four tonal registers: H, L and HL (falling) and LH (rising).
tn.cite: Koni Muluwa, Joseph. 2010. Plantes, animaux et champignons en langues bantu: étude comparée de phytonymes, zoonymes et myconymes en nsong, ngong, mpiin, mbuun et hungan (Bandundu, RD Congo). Thèse de doctorat, Université Libre de Bruxelles, Faculté de Philosophie et Lettres (promoteurs K. Bostoen et A. Shango Mutambwe; soutenue le 28 juin 2010), 559 pp.
tn.locator: p. 53, section 1.1.3.2 Systeme tonal mbuun; TBU sentence p. 49, section 1.1.3
tn.note: Two level tones H/L; falling and rising treated as H+L / L+H on one syllable nucleus but listed as four 'registres tonals'; tonal minimal pairs given (oka 'poil' vs 'serpent'); nothing on stress. Checked against the source (tone consistency check round 3, 2026-09-24): system level-or-register -> level-and-contour (p. 53, section 1.1.3.2 Système tonal mbuun).

corr.words: Ces tons modulés résultent des contacts entre deux tons simples. ... nous pensons que le mbuun a quatre registres tonals: H, B et HB (descendant) et BH (montant). ... Néanmoins, dans la mesure où il existe des noms avec ce ton montant, même s'ils sont rarissimes ou ne s'opposent à rien d'autre, nous considérons ce registre.

5619.loc: p. 116, section 三 声调 + p. 117, section 四 结语
5619.idn: Name in the source: 古缅语; “妙齐提”碑文时期缅语; 十二世纪初缅甸语

tn.quote: 在“妙齐提”碑文时期，只有元音长短之分还没有高平调出现，如果说，元音长短区别音位，可把它们算作声调。那么当时只有两个声调，一个短调，一个长调。妙碑中反映出来在古缅语中，有着较丰富的声母系统和辅音韵尾系统，因而声调的区别作用幷不突出，字音的高低变化，只是一种伴随特征。幷不具备音位功能。[p.117] 关于声调，我们的结论是：古缅语中只有长、短两调。后来的四个声调是历史发展的结果。[a']尾、[h]尾是分别表示短调和长调的一种符号。
tn.translation: In the period of the Myazedi inscription there was only a distinction of vowel length; no high-level tone had yet appeared. If one takes vowel length as phonemically distinctive, one may count them as tones; then there were only two tones at the time, a short tone and a long tone. As the inscription shows, Old Burmese had a fairly rich system of initials and consonant codas, so the distinguishing role of tone was not prominent; variation in the pitch of syllables was only a concomitant feature and had no phonemic function. ... On tone, our conclusion is: Old Burmese had only two 'tones', long and short. The later four tones are the result of historical development. …
tn.cite: 汪大年 [Wang Danian]. 1986. 妙齐提碑文研究(一)——十二世纪初缅甸语音初探 [A study of the Myazedi inscription (1): a first look at early-12th-century Burmese phonology]. 北京大学学报(哲学社会科学版) 1986(4): 103-118.
tn.locator: p. 116, section 三 声调 + p. 117, section 四 结语
tn.note: Author posits only a long vs short vowel-length '调' contrast, pitch explicitly non-phonemic; coded as no tone. One could instead record 2 length 'tones' (短调, 长调). Argued from inscription spellings. Quotation re-keyed from the printed page on 2026-09-24.

tn.quote: As was mentioned earlier, KiYaka has three phonetic tones: L, H, and R. To account for the different surface tonal phenomena, I propose that KiYaka has basically the H-L opposition supplemented by accent. The H is specified underlyingly and can be prelinked or floating, but the L is supplied by default according to the following rule: … As for the R, I suggest that it is just the phonetic realisation of H on accented syllables. Specifically, the H is converted into R by the following phonetic rule. (13) H-RAISING: Realise an accented syllable linked to H as R.
